extracted.intended_audience: Apple users, tech-industry observers, app developers, and tech journalists
extracted.subtask_description: A short-form opinion / analysis about Apple Intelligence's notification-summarization feature, its problems (misleading AI summaries), and suggested policy / UX fixes. Aimed at readers interested in product design, privacy, and news integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear labeling of AI-generated summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple should 'further clarify when the text being displayed is summarization provided by Apple Intelligence' and 'it really ought to be crystal clear what is an Apple-Intelligence-generated summary and what is not.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labels must make it unambiguous to recipients that a notification is an AI-generated summary rather than the publisher's original text; the clarification should be obvious enough for ordinary users, not just those who know to look for a subtle cue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility and understandability of the summary icon/glyph
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification summaries are 'marked with an icon/glyph... a clever icon to convey an abstract concept' whose 'meaning... is not at all obvious unless you know to look for it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The icon or glyph used to mark summaries should be readily interpretable by typical users; relying on a subtle Unicode-like glyph that users won't notice is an anti-pattern. Consider more explicit visual/ textual indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about 'beta' status in marketing and promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: All of Apple Intelligence is labelled 'beta'. People generally know what 'beta' means. Yet 'Apple is promoting the hell out of Apple Intelligence' and its advertisements 'hide, rather than emphasize, its "beta" quality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a feature is experimental or likely to produce errors, promotional materials should not obscure that fact; promotion is an implicit encouragement to use the feature, so marketing should prominently communicate limitations and risk of errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: User opt-in and user controls for enabling summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple Intelligence 'has to be opted into, and once enabled, can be turned off.' Users control feature enablement and which apps are exempt via 'Settings → Notifications → Summarize Notifications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain explicit user opt-in and easy-to-find controls to disable the feature or exempt specific apps; placing control with users (rather than silently applying summaries) aligns with expectations about inbox/notification filtering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developer opt-out / app-level opt-out option
rubrics_metrics.description: What's 'conspicuously missing' is 'a way for individual app developers to opt out of it. For a developer to say, effectively, "Never offer summaries of this app's notifications."' This would alleviate some problems, though not all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an API or setting allowing app developers (especially news publishers) to request that their app's notifications never be summarized. Note limitations: some notifications are proxied through other apps (email, aggregators), so a developer opt-out won't solve every case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce error rate; ensure high reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: While 'the mistake rate is very low and the utility is very high,' Apple Intelligence 'really needs to reduce the number of these errors'—egregious mistakes (e.g., false claims about suicides or event winners) are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize improvements to summarization accuracy and safety; measure and minimize harms from hallucinations or incorrect factual claims. The tolerance for errors should be lower than for typical internal beta features because mistakes can impersonate publishers and mislead readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish AI summaries from verbatim original notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: It must be clear 'what is an AI-generated summary and what is a verbatim original notification.' Users should not reasonably presume an AI summary is original publisher content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit textual markers or formatting (not just an icon) and/or brief explanatory text to indicate summaries are generated, so recipients do not mistake them for the publisher's own reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make reporting unexpected or problematic summaries easy
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple's statement encourages users 'to report a concern if they view an unexpected notification summary.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement straightforward 'report' flows from the notification itself (or immediately reachable from it) so users can flag misinformation or harmful summaries quickly; use reports to improve models and remediate harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify notification ownership and policy priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The author asks 'To whom do notifications belong—the developer... or the user who is receiving them?' and outlines a rule of thumb: Apple's priorities are 'Apple itself. Users. Developers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy decisions (e.g., whether developers can opt out) should be informed by a clear model of ownership and priority; the stated prioritization (Apple > Users > Developers) explains why Apple may leave controls with users, but the tradeoffs should be transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain the feature but fix clarity and safety issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls to entirely remove the feature are dismissed as 'hysterical nonsense.' The appropriate path is to 'further clarify' labeling and reduce errors rather than wholesale removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance the demonstrated high utility of summaries against their harms; prefer incremental fixes (better labeling, opt-outs, reporting, accuracy improvements) over removing a useful feature.
